questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks need drain valves. These valves remove oil and water that collect in the tanks. They can work manually or automatically.

questions.question: Most drivers are least alert:
questions.correctAnswerText: At night.
questions.explanation: Tiredness and poor alertness are serious dangers at night. Most people are least alert at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: When coupling two trailers, you can secure the second trailer by:

options.text: Backing the trailer into a wall.
Placing wheel chocks on the sides of the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Setting the trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: If you attach a second trailer without spring brakes, set the emergency brakes. Connect the emergency lines between both trailers, fill the air tank, then disconnect the lines. This sets the emergency brakes if the slack adjusters are properly set.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to be running.
questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: To avoid aggressive driving, you should:

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Not make gestures to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make gestures to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan trips with realistic time and extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane. Do not make any gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is recommended because:

options.text: The driver has the best view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help from the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver has the best view.
questions.explanation: When backing, drivers should back toward the left side. This gives the driver the best view of the rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts because:

options.text: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first begins. Rain mixes with oil and grease on the road to create a slippery layer. As the rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: Avoid sudden lane changes by:

options.text: Using your horn to push other drivers out of your lane.
Only driving slower than the speed limit.
Pulling off the road during heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous. Avoid them by looking ahead for obstacles that require you to change lanes.

questions.question: Shut-off valves:

options.text: Stop air from leaving air brake systems.
Stop air from entering air brake systems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. Keep the rear shut-off valve closed to prevent air from leaving the brake system.

questions.question: In wet conditions, no spray from other vehicles' tires means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
Spray is trapped under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, no spray from other vehicles' tires means ice has formed. Drive carefully in wet, cold weather.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent fatigue while driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the cab cool.
questions.explanation: A warm, poorly ventilated cab makes you sleepy. Opening a window, vent, or using air conditioning keeps the cab cool and helps prevent fatigue.

questions.question: When does a large combination vehicle take the longest time to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: When empty.
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. Less weight means the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: What is true about hearing trains near a railroad crossing?

options.text: You will hear every approaching train.
You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
You will hear two short blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
questions.explanation: Never assume you will hear an approaching train. The operator may not sound the horn, or horns may be prohibited in that area. Noise inside your vehicle may also prevent you from hearing a train until it is dangerously close.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid blocking traffic when driving a heavy vehicle?

options.text: Try to pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Ride the brakes while driving downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane.
questions.explanation: If your heavy vehicle cannot match the speed of other traffic, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: Which shut-off valves should be open during a trip?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: Before starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches all brakes and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: When should you test the low pressure warning signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Test your low pressure warning light before each trip. After the system charges, press and release the brake pedal quickly to release air. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: A single air brake system with two sets of controls.
One air brake system for each side of the truck.
Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that use one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems with a single set of brake controls. One system operates the rear axle brakes. The other operates the front axle brakes.

questions.question: What role do gauges play during a trip?

options.text: They are the only way to learn of vehicle problems.
They help you learn of possible vehicle problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you learn of possible vehicle problems.
questions.explanation: During a trip, regularly check gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for signs of trouble.

questions.question: Which name does NOT describe a convex mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Flat side mirror
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are also called fisheye, spot, or bug-eye mirrors. Flat side mirrors are different.

questions.question: What happens if you unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer?

options.text: The tow bar may cause injury.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tow bar may cause injury.
questions.explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer. The dolly tow bar could fly up and cause serious injury.
